name: flying-button

frames.best_why: The button sits evenly lit at rest with both thruster pods visible and no cursor over the label.

tagline: A dark pill button with two small thruster pods under its edge.
summary: A rounded charcoal call-to-action reading Launch project, with two little engine pods beneath it. The recording only shows it at rest; the code is built to lift it on a jet of smoke when hovered.
appearance: A long dark-charcoal pill with softly rounded ends sits centred on black, the white label inside and a faint light sheen across its top edge. Two small grey tabs poke out beneath the lower rim like tiny engine nozzles.
behaviour: In every frame the button stays still: the pointer moves onto it and the hand cursor appears, but nothing lifts and no smoke or flame is emitted. In the source, hovering is meant to fire thruster columns and fly the button upward, carrying a drawn cursor with it.
search_phrases: rocket button for a landing page
use_when: A playful launch or submit button on a marketing page that can afford a moment of theatre.
avoid_when: The button leaves its place and hides the cursor, so it is a poor fit for touch or critical forms.
customise: Pass the label as children and set size, theme, radius, altitude, hover time, jet count, trigger mode and the optional ramp track. Thruster, smoke, button and text colours are props too.
weight_why: A grid fluid simulation runs advection, pressure and dye passes plus a smoke shader each frame.

a11y.note: The label stays a real button with a focus ring, but liftoff is hover-driven and the cursor is hidden while flying.

issues: No frame shows liftoff, smoke or a flame, even with the pointer resting on the button.
The thruster pods look like small grey tabs and are easy to miss at rest.
polish_why: The pill is cleanly drawn but flat and plain, and the engine detail barely reads at rest.
title: Flying Button
